Example models

Source: R/data-example_models.R
example_models.Rd

Two example models: a small capacity-expansion LP written with the multimod constructors, and the energyRt energy system model, both as GAMS source text and as the multimod model parsed from it with data attached.

Usage

example_models

Format

A list with 2 elements:

toy

A two-region capacity-expansion LP (3 technologies, 2 regions, 4 parameters, 3 variables, 3 equations) written with the multimod constructors in data-raw/toy_model.R. Every parameter carries data, so model_to_lp() gives a 9 x 13 LP and solve_highs() finds the optimum (198000).

energyRt

The energyRt model on the TOPIA test case:

gams

List with model: energyRt's GAMS template source (gams/energyRt.gms) as a character vector, ready for read_gams(include = FALSE).

multimod

The multimod model parsed from that source, with data from an interpolated energyRt scenario attached.

metadata

List with source, scenario, repository, license, energyRt_version, gams_source, date_imported, note.

Source

  • energyRt: https://github.com/optimal2050/energyRt

Details

energyRt is an R package for energy system modeling. The TOPIA R7 kit is a seven-region test case with a seasonal timeslice calendar.

The model structure is parsed from energyRt's GAMS template with read_gams(include = FALSE); the data is attached from an interpolated energyRt scenario. See data-raw/build_energyRt_fixture.R in the source repository.

License: the energyRt content is distributed under the Apache License 2.0, the license of multimod itself. See the COPYRIGHTS file installed with the package, system.file("COPYRIGHTS", package = "multimod").

See also

  • read_gams for parsing GAMS models

  • read_gmpl for parsing MathProg models

  • as_multimod for converting model structures to multimod

Examples

names(example_models)
#> [1] "energyRt" "toy"     
names(example_models$energyRt)
#> [1] "gams"     "multimod" "metadata"
example_models$energyRt$metadata
#> $source
#> [1] "energyRt TOPIA kit"
#> 
#> $scenario
#> [1] "R7 / topia_seasons / base horizon"
#> 
#> $repository
#> [1] "https://github.com/optimal2050/energyRt"
#> 
#> $license
#> [1] "Apache-2.0"
#> 
#> $energyRt_version
#> [1] "0.90.0.9012"
#> 
#> $gams_source
#> [1] "gams/energyRt.gms"
#> 
#> $date_imported
#> [1] "2026-10-04"
#> 
#> $note
#> [1] "Model structure parsed from energyRt's GAMS template with read_gams(include = FALSE); data attached from an interpolated energyRt scenario. See data-raw/build_energyRt_fixture.R."
#> 

# the small model built in R
example_models$toy
#> Model: toy
#> Description: two-region capacity expansion toy model
#> Language:  multimod 
#> Sets:  2 
#> Mappings:  2 
#> Aliases:  0 
#> Parameters:  4 
#> Variables:  3 
#> Equations:  3 

# the parsed energyRt model
example_models$energyRt$multimod
#> Model: 
#> Source:  C:/Users/admin/Documents/R/energyRt/gams/energyRt.gms 
#> Language:  GAMS 
#> Sets:  27 
#> Mappings:  324 
#> Aliases:  7 
#> Parameters:  218 
#> Variables:  93 
#> Equations:  153 

# \donttest{
# parse the structure again from the bundled GAMS source
structure <- read_gams(
  file_or_text = example_models$energyRt$gams$model,
  include = FALSE
)
# }
